This study aims to characterize the impact of increasing water temperatures on IHNV replication and host-pathogen interactions. Following pre-screening, the replication kinetics of the reference strain N61 and two field isolates RtNag0a and SA-22 were characterized in EPC (Epithelioma Papulosum Cyprini) and RTG-2 (Rainbow trout gonad) cell lines at 14, 20 and 22{degrees}. Virulence and host-pathogen interactions were subsequently investigated in vivo in zebrafish (Zf) larvae using complementary microinjection and bath immersion infection models at 21.5 and 23.5{degrees}. In vitro studies revealed distinct thermal replication profiles, distinguishing thermosensitive from thermotolerant isolates, although these phenotypes were influenced by the cellular environment. The zebrafish model enabled the characterization of virulence and antiviral host responses associated with thermotolerant IHNV isolates. Notably, waterborne infection proved effective, contrasting with previous reports describing this exposure route as unsuitable for IHNV studies. These findings expand the growing list of emerging European IHNV genotypes capable of replicating at elevated temperatures (>20{degrees}) and establish zebrafish larvae as a relevant model for virulence assessment of field isolates. Together, these results provide valuable insights into the potential impact of climate warming on IHNV epidemiology and support efforts to predict and anticipate future outbreaks under changing environmental conditions.
papers.title: Epidemic Risks associated with high-temperature replicating infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) field isolates: from molecular characterization to host pathogen interactions

papers.abstract: In November 2025, the first global H5N5 infection was reported in a person in Washington State. Previously, these viruses had only been detected in seabirds and shorebirds near the Atlantic Ocean, suggesting potentially distinct ecology from dominant H5N1 strains. Using 354 global H5N5 genomes, we show that H5N5 viruses have been carried by high latitude seabirds and shorebirds across the Atlantic at least 9 times, with introductions more frequent in the fall and spring. We reconstruct a plausible path of cross-continental movement via Arctic or sub-Arctic regions, followed by a year of cryptic circulation prior to human spillover. These data show that H5N5 viruses have undergone far more intercontinental movements than previously recognized, and exhibit host and geographic patterns that are fundamentally distinct from dominant H5N1 lineages. The distinct host ecology, geography, and movement, paired with the capacity to infect a person, suggest that enhanced surveillance may be warranted.
papers.title: H5N5 virus transmission is driven by repeated cross-Atlantic introductions and transmission among high latitude seabirds

papers.abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) are standard care for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance limits their durability, and alternatives that do not depend on EGFR kinase activity are needed. We asked whether inhibitors of SF3b, a core component of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle, act on NSCLC cells regardless of EGFR genotype. Three lung adenocarcinoma lines were treated with pladienolide B or herboxidiene at 0.01, 0.1 and 1 uM: PC9 and HCC827, both carrying an EGFR exon 19 deletion and both inhibited by gefitinib at nanomolar concentrations, and A549, which is EGFR wild type and gefitinibin sensitive. Proliferation was followed for three days by crystal violet staining, EGFR intron 2 retention was assayed by RTPCR, and EGFR protein was measured by western blotting. Both compounds produced a concentration-dependent increase in the intron 2 retained product in all three lines, and both held proliferation at or near the day 0 cell number in all three, at concentrations down to 0.01 uM. EGFR protein was lost in PC9, reduced in A549, and only partly reduced in HCC827, where a residual band persisted in lanes whose growth was fully suppressed. Since A549 is EGFR wild-type, and published knockdown data show that removing EGFR does not suppress proliferation of wild-type lines, the growth inhibition cannot be attributed to loss of EGFR alone. We read EGFR intron 2 retention as a marker of target engagement rather than as the mechanism of the growth effect. These are the results of single experiments without replicates or statistical testing and should be read as preliminary.
papers.title: SF3b inhibitors suppress proliferation of nonsmall cell lung cancer cells irrespective of EGFR mutation status

papers.abstract: Temporal asynchrony within a vegetation period, such as when mixing trees with contrasting leaf phenology (i.e. deciduous and evergreen species), may play an important role in accelerating belowground nutrient cycling in mixed-species forests. However, forests are increasingly impacted by drought, and how mixing effects may be modified by changes in water availability is unknown. Using an 11-year-old experimental plantation in southwestern France, we tested the interactive effect of stand composition (monocultures of each Pinus pinaster and Betula pendula, and the mixture of the two species) and water availability (via irrigation) on various belowground processes. We quantified soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability with ion-exchange resins in the growing vs dormant periods, net mineralization with an in situ soil incubation method every 4-6 weeks from April to September, and N uptake by trees using two in situ 15N soil labeling campaigns, one at budburst and one at peak leaf expansion in summer. The methods were implemented at several time points, in order to elucidate potential temporal complementarity in the mixture. We found differences in soil nutrient availability between different species compositions, with pure pine generally having higher mineral N, and pure birch having higher available P under high water availability. These differences were unlikely due to increases in net nutrient mineralization, as these rates were similar among treatments. Instead, differences in tree growth and canopy covering between species compositions, and thus different nutrient uptake needs may be the main drivers for the soil nutrient availability trends. The 15N labeling experiment revealed a competitive advantage for pine in the mixture at budburst, with higher N uptake than pine in monocultures, without negatively impacting birch uptake. This advantage was then lost once birch's leaves were out in the early summer. We conclude that the timing of nutrient needs and uptake of species within a mixture, such as between a broadleaf deciduous and an evergreen conifer, may be a stronger driver than mineralization for soil nutrient availability in a mixture, even under two contrasted levels of water availability.
papers.title: Tree species composition and nutrient uptake influence soil nutrient availability, even under contrasted levels of water availability

papers.abstract: Current knowledge of DNA packaging in eukaryotic nuclei largely centers on its basic unit, the nucleosome. Multiple lineages have, however, diverged from this paradigm, most notably dinoflagellates. Among other molecular oddities, these enigmatic protists have enormous genomes, permanently condensed chromosomes and a foreign gene encoding Dinoflagellate Viral Nucleoprotein (DVNP), which is used for packing DNA. Some dinoflagellates also have Histone-like Proteins (HLPs) acquired from bacteria via lateral gene transfer. Dinoflagellates were long thought to lack histones entirely, but canonical histone genes have been identified by transcriptomics. Here, we performed proteomics on purified nuclei and confirmed the presence of all four core histone classes, along with variants, and DVNP in the dinoflagellates Oxyrrhis marina and Amphidinium carterae and HLPs in A. carterae. We also identified putative histone post-translational modifications found in canonical eukaryotes. Comparative genomics of dinoflagellates revealed histone-handling and modification machinery alongside an apparent reduction in, or diversification of, machinery responsible for replication-dependent nucleosome deposition (CAF-1), consistent with a predominantly transcription-associated role for nucleosomes. Furthermore, proteomics revealed modifications of DVNP and HLP, raising the possibility of machinery co-opting. These observations support a new model of a dinoflagellate chromatin that includes the localization of canonical nucleosomes to insulated chromatin territories (INTs).
papers.title: Proteomics reveals conserved features of histone biology in dinoflagellates

papers.abstract: Climate-associated genomic variation is often used as a proxy for adaptive potential, yet whether it reflects adaptation with phenotypic consequences, rather than demography alone, is rarely tested in long-lived species. Genomic offsets forecast climate maladaptation from genotype-environment models but are seldom validated against phenotypes. We combined whole-genome resequencing, SNP and transposable element insertion polymorphism (TIP) variation, landscape genomics, genome-wide association, genomic offset, and common-garden phenotyping in the European wild apple (Malus sylvestris Mill.), a crop wild relative with a complex demographic history, to test this. Results: Of 148 resequenced accessions (135 wild, 13 cultivated), 89 wild individuals formed the core dataset. Population structure was associated with Last Glacial Maximum precipitation rather than contemporary climate, and genetic diversity increased from west to east. Genome-environment associations across 9.75 million SNPs identified climate-associated loci enriched in photoperiod-related flowering-time genes, with limited overlap with phenotype-associated loci. SNP-based genomic offset was associated with bud-break timing in the Saclay common garden (marginal R2 = 0.31), with higher offsets corresponding to earlier bud break, but not with growth or ecophysiological traits. This association depended on Austrian and Romanian populations and was clearest in non-admixed wild individuals. Offsets based on TIPs or glacial climate did not predict measured phenotypes. Conclusions: Climate association, phenotypic relevance, and predictive power of genomic variation are separable. In a long-lived tree, genomic offset predicted spring phenology, a key adaptive trait, but this signal varied across provenances and ancestries and was absent for transposable elements. Genomic offsets can therefore forecast potential phenological maladaptation, provided they are validated against phenotypes such as bud break.
papers.title: Genomic forecasting links climate-associated variation to spring phenology in the European wild apple, a crop wild relative of the cultivated apple

papers.abstract: During twilight, flying male Photinus fireflies flash in search for conspecific females, which sit on the vegetation below and flash back in response. However, before darkness sets in, the green vegetation in the habitat makes the detection of flashes more difficult. Twilight active fireflies tend to emit more yellow flashes than nocturnal fireflies and it has been proposed that firefly flash colour evolved to enhance the contrast of firefly flashes against their signalling background. There is indirect evidence for this contrast hypothesis, but it remains to be rigorously tested. This is the first study to directly test the contrast hypothesis by recording ambient light spectra in three different habitats throughout the daily flash activity of Photinus pyralis and P. australis and comparing these ambient light spectra to the male flash spectra of the two species. The contrast hypothesis predicts that during peak activity, firefly light colour will maximally contrast with the signalling background. Our data show that male flash spectra fit into a gap in the ambient light spectrum that opens during peak flashing activity of each species, effectively enhancing the visual contrast between male flashes and their background and making males more visible to their potential mates.
papers.title: How to stand out to a mate - Flash colour of Photinus fireflies maximizes signal contrast against ambient light

papers.abstract: Inhibitory networks shape information processing in the brain by integrating signals across space, regulating neuronal responses, and controlling the flow of signals through neural circuits. Understanding these computations requires linking the structure of individual inhibitory neuron types to their functional properties and network connectivity. The retina provides a tractable system for meeting this challenge, yet the organization of many retinal inhibitory circuits remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a population of polyaxonal amacrine cells recorded using multielectrode arrays as A1 amacrine cells, a morphologically defined interneuron type in primate retina. This identification is supported by a correspondence between properties of morphologically-identified A1 cells from single cell recordings and putative A1 amacrines in the array recordings. We then identified recursive bistratified ganglion cells in the array recordings based on their electrical coupling to A1 cells, linking this inhibitory network to retinal output pathways. A1 and recursive bistratified cells also share an asymmetry in receptive-field organization, with larger On than Off centers. Finally, A1 spike amplitudes decline during bursts, and analyses of their electrical images suggest that this change may cause some spikes to fail to propagate through their extensive axonal arbors. These findings establish the cellular identity and network organization of a long-range inhibitory circuit in the primate retina and reveal how neuronal architecture, connectivity, and spike dynamics may jointly shape the transmission of visual information.
papers.title: Polyaxonal A1 amacrine cells form a spatially extended network in primate retina

papers.abstract: N-glycosylation generates substantial molecular diversity, yet how glycan composition varies throughout aging remains poorly understood. We mapped the N-glycoproteome of brain, liver, spleen, kidney, and plasma across nine ages spanning the mouse lifespan, identifying 80,618 unique N-glycopeptides at 9,211 glycosites on 4,391 glycoproteins, together with matched proteomic trajectories (glycoproteinatlas.org). Organ identity was the dominant determinant of glycan composition, but numerous glycosites nevertheless underwent remodeling with age. The brain showed a prominent age-associated increase in short paucimannose glycans, driven in part by the age-associated increase in the glycan-processing enzyme HEXB. In white matter, a hotspot for this change, aging increased the paucimannosylation of Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), a major target of central nervous system autoimmunity. We identified MOG-reactive autoantibodies in aged individuals and patients with MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and showed that the glycan at MOG N60 modulates autoantibody binding. Experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) recapitulated a subset of the age-associated glycosite changes, revealing shared glycosylation signatures between aging and autoimmune targeting of MOG. Together, these findings reveal site-specific N-glycosylation as both a marker of age and a regulator of molecular interactions.
papers.title: An atlas of the aging glycoproteome reveals how glycosylation modulates autoantibody binding in the brain

papers.abstract: The soapberry bug Jadera haematoloma is a classic model of rapid adaptive evolution, with a well-documented host shift from native herbaceous sapinds to the introduced goldenrain tree (Koelreuteria spp.). This host shift has facilitated the insect's spread into novel anthropogenic urban habitats. Microbial associations are often critical to insect environmental adaptation. Here, we characterize the gut microbiota of J. haematoloma across native and introduced host plants, seasonal transitions, and a gradient of urbanicity. Our findings indicate that the soapberry bug gut microbiome is highly specialized, with a small number of core bacterial amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) primarily from the families Rhizobiaceae, Streptococcaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, and Lactobacillaceae. While traits such as sex and wing morph do not correlate with microbiome structure, the host plant acts as the primary determinant of community composition. Bugs feeding on the ancestral host plant maintain a more diverse and even microbial community featuring Enterobacteriaceae, whereas the gut environment of bugs on the introduced host is overwhelmingly dominated by a single unclassified Rhizobiaceae ASV. Furthermore, seasonal transitions drive significant turnover among accessory microbial taxa. Finally, we demonstrate that urbanization introduces a distinct ecological effect on the insect's microbiome. While the degree of local green space does not systematically alter within-host taxonomic richness, it is associated with modest change in mean community composition and significantly disrupts microbial community variance. Increased urbanization correlates with significantly higher beta dispersion, indicating that anthropogenic environments lead to more stochastic microbiomes, which may be an indicator of environmental stress. Together, these results illustrate how rapid dietary host shifts and the ecological pressures of urbanization interact to shape the microbiome of a synanthropic insect.
papers.title: Host specificity, seasonality, and urbanicity shape the gut microbiome of a synanthropic insect

papers.abstract: Fungal plant diseases are a major cause of crop loss worldwide. Understanding the processes driving these diseases is therefore crucial to anticipate and control epidemics while improving crop yield production. Moreover, the new European Green Deal aims to reduce the use of pesticides, while, few alternatives are currently available on the market. There is therefore an urgent need to better track and anticipate fungal crop epidemics in the current context of fungicide reduction. In light of this, our study aims to understand Fusarium spill overs from non-agricultural habitats in order to better characterise potential non-host Fusarium reservoirs that may be implicated in the emergence of Fusarium diseases. To address this question, we isolated Fusarium lineages from natural populations of Brassica rapa. We characterised their phylogenomic affiliation and found that they display high diversity, with a population structure related to the locality of isolation. By inoculation assays, we identified Fusarium strains from non-agricultural habitats that were highly aggressive on wheat. In addition, we observed a strong effect of wheat variety on disease development. We monitored the Fusarium colonisation through a microscopy approach in both wheat and Brassica plants. We observed that while the fungus is mostly on root surface in Brassica plants, it spreads inter-cellularly in wheat roots with vascular colonisation in the wheat shoots. Finally, we showed that most aggressive Fusarium strains were isolated from Brittany, a French region where wheat is vastly cultivated.
papers.title: Natural habitats are reservoirs of Fusarium lineages highly pathogenic on Triticum aestivum

papers.abstract: Beetles of the family Passalidae are an important group of subsocial wood-decomposing (saproxylophagous) insects, spending their entire life cycle living inside and feeding on rotten logs. Decaying wood is an abundant resource, but nutritionally poor and challenging to digest. As in other saproxylophagous insects, digestion for passalids is only possible through symbiotic relationships with their gut microbiota, highlighting the critical roles of these symbionts in the evolution of wood-decomposing insects. Despite its importance, this critical symbiotic relationship remains poorly understood, hindering our ability to identify the factors shaping this association and assessing its role in the evolution of Passalidae. Using high-throughput sequencing of the microbial 16S rRNA we comparatively analyzed the composition and abundance of symbiont lineages in the anterior hindguts of passalid beetles from two independent mountain systems in the Colombian Caribbean region. We tested the influence of geographical co-occurrence and phylogenetic relatedness on gut microbial composition and structure. We posit that if shared locality was the primary driver of gut microbiome assembly, then sympatric species should harbor more similar microbiomes regardless of their phylogenetic relationships. Alternatively, if host evolutionary history is the dominant factor, congeneric species should exhibit more similar microbiomes regardless of geographic co-occurrence. Our results support that phylogenetic relatedness explained substantially more variation in both bacterial and archaeal communities than geographic locality, indicating that gut microbiome composition is primarily structured by host evolutionary history. Furthermore, bacterial and archaeal communities exhibited evidence of phylosymbiosis, although at different phylogenetic scales: bacterial communities more closely reflected relationships among genus level clades, whereas archaeal communities retained congruence mainly at deeper host lineages. We also uncovered extensive bacterial taxonomic novelty, with nearly half of bacterial reads remaining unclassified at the genus level, highlighting the large undescribed microbial diversity associated with Passalidae. These findings lead to establishing Passalidae as a promising comparative model for investigating the evolutionary processes governing gut microbiome assembly and the evolution of lignocellulose-feeding symbioses.
papers.title: Termite-Like Phylogenetic Conservation of Gut Microbiota in Passalid Beetles Suggests Evolutionary Convergence in Decaying Wood Degradation

papers.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variants, whether maternally inherited or acquired somatically during aging, can be particularly detrimental to cells that rely on mitochondrial metabolism such as neurons. The functional consequences of mtDNA variants are thought to depend on their heteroplasmy, defined as the proportion of mtDNA molecules carrying that variant. However, investigating the specific effects of heteroplasmic mtDNA variants on human neuronal function has been challenging. Studies using patient-derived cells cannot conclusively attribute observed phenotypes to a single mtDNA variant, while conventional genome editing approaches are not applicable to mtDNA. Here, we use DddA-derived cytosine base editor (DdCBE) to introduce pathogenic heteroplasmic mtDNA variants into Neurogenin 2 (NGN2)-inducible human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). We focus on two variants in the genes MT-ND1 and MT-ND5 belonging to complex I (CI), the largest component of the mitochondrial respiratory chain and a frequent contributor to human disease, including the incurable neurodevelopmental disorder Leigh syndrome. mtDNA-edited iPSC lines exhibit low off-target editing and maintain similar heteroplasmy following subclonal isolation and differentiation into NGN2-induced neurons (iNs). Although the CI variants do not substantially affect mitochondrial energy metabolism in undifferentiated iPSCs, they reduce mitochondrial membrane potential in iNs where they drive a transcriptional reprogramming indicative of impaired neuronal commitment. These findings suggest that heteroplasmic CI variants are sufficient to disrupt neural fate specification even at relatively low heteroplasmy. More broadly, mtDNA editing in human iPSCs provides a powerful platform to investigate how mitochondrial fitness and heteroplasmy influence development and disease.
papers.title: Mitochondrial genome editing reveals the impact of complex I heteroplasmic variants on human neurogenesis

papers.abstract: Restoration of protected areas should aim to maximize outcomes for both biological conservation and local people's livelihoods. In rural Africa, livelihoods are inextricably linked to the provision of ecosystem services (ES) from natural resources, so that community-centred biodiversity conservation must be guided by local perceptions of ES. Our study examined perceptions of ES among eight communities within a 5-km radius of a Nigerian forest reserve characterized by an elevational gradient of 700 m, spanning montane forest, mid-elevation forest, and savannah. The montane forest is noted for its outstanding biodiversity value. We employed semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions and species-use inventories to characterize which ES are recognised, and their perceived importance. We also conducted an ethnobotanical assessment to document community uses of plants and classified the species as savannah or forest species. Across settlements, we observed a three-fold variation in the number of ES recognized, ranging from 6 to 20. Provisioning services, especially food, were ranked higher than regulating, cultural, or supporting services in most settlements. Notably, most provisioning services were from savannah, rather than forest species. Our study adds to growing data on indigenous knowledge about ecosystem services. Implications from these findings are that: i) Landscape-scale management should maintain a mosaic of montane forest and derived savannah to reflect prevailing provisioning needs while enhancing regulating and supporting services. ii) Restoration should prioritise tangible provisioning benefits (e.g., non-timber forest products, medicines and food) alongside regulating and supporting services to align with local priorities. iii) Given potential trade-offs between scientifically derived valuations (biodiversity, regulation) and stakeholder priorities, co-design of restoration objectives and adaptive governance are essential to secure local buy-in and on-going stewardship.
papers.title: Indigenous communities' perceptions of ecosystem services of a montane forest ecosystem in Nigeria: Implications for restoration planning

papers.abstract: Avian influenza virus H5N1 is predominantly found in wild and domestic birds. H5N1 genotype B3.13 was first detected in United States dairy cattle in March 2024 and spread through much of the country during 2024 and 2025, resulting in the largest known H5N1 outbreak in domestic mammals. By analysing viral genomic data jointly with historical cattle movement patterns, we find that live cattle movement is the predominant contributor to H5N1 spatial spread, rather than wild or domestic birds. Using phylogeographic methods we estimate that >40% of interstate viral transmissions occurred before B3.13's first detection and >70% occurred before interstate dairy cattle movement restrictions were implemented in April 2024. After this implementation, interstate transmission slowed but within-state spread persisted, driven by local cattle network density and movement volume. Our epidemic simulations demonstrate that the connectivity of counties within and around the Texas Panhandle - where the earliest cases were documented - predisposed the region to become an outbreak epicentre. Counterfactual simulations indicate that interstate restrictions needed to have begun 2-3 months earlier in order to limit the epizootic substantively, given the extent of cryptic spread before detection. Network-informed interventions outperformed geographically-defined containment, but response speed (rather than intervention strength) was the limiting factor in our epidemic models, underscoring the need for surveillance systems capable of detecting pathogen emergence before widespread dissemination.
papers.title: Dairy cattle movement networks govern the spread and persistence of H5N1 B3.13 in the United States

papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are trained mostly on human and other vertebrate cells, yet are proposed as general-purpose models. Whether they transfer far beyond their training species is unknown. We evaluated zero-shot embeddings from Geneformer, scGPT and UCE against PCA and scVI in developmental atlases of Dictyostelium discoideum and Caenorhabditis elegans, separated from humans by 1.2 billion and 600 million years. Without retraining, the models recovered developmental order and preserved organism-specific cell identities. UCE encodes genes by protein sequence and could use 97% of measured genes, whereas Geneformer and scGPT, after ortholog mapping, used under one-fifth. UCE performed most consistently, often exceeding species-native baselines. Restricted to ortholog-mappable genes, it still scored above vocabulary-based models on five of six annotation tasks, some narrowly. Foundation models can thus yield informative cell embeddings across more than a billion years of evolution, and protein-sequence gene representations make these embeddings more complete and often more accurate.
papers.title: Single-cell foundation models transfer across deep evolutionary distances

papers.abstract: In highly variable ecosystems, natural variability can obscure signals of decline that warrant intervention, as there is often a lack of long-term data needed to distinguish between declines that are transient and likely to recover naturally and those that would be permanent without intervention. Implementing restoration for a species involves deciding on a threshold condition at which to intervene, duration that this threshold needs to be met before intervening, life stages at introduction, and amounts to introduce. Current bull and giant kelp restoration efforts in California were spurred by persistent kelp loss that started in 2013 following a disease outbreak among predators of the primary herbivore and a marine heatwave. We asked how decisions about intervention cue, threshold, wait time, life stage at introduction, and amount affect population outcomes against a backdrop of environmental variability. We analyzed additional context-dependencies on grazing and climate intensity. To address these questions, we built and parameterized a stochastic stage-structured model for bull and giant kelp, in which we simulated kelp enhancement approaches under a range of grazing and climate scenarios. In a global sensitivity analysis of kelp enhancement decisions, we found that grazing intensity and life stages at introduction were the most influential determinants of kelp biomass and persistence outcomes. The kelp enhancement approach involving temporarily introduced juveniles restored the germ banks of bull and giant kelp, but the two species differed in their responses to that intervention, highlighting that optimal intervention approach is species-dependent. Waiting longer for natural recovery before intervening reduced total intervention effort but also reduced biomass recovery potential. These results support empirical findings from kelp enhancement pilot projects in California and highlight context-dependencies that inform restoration decision-making in kelp forests and other highly variable ecosystems.
papers.title: Restoration decisions in highly variable systems: Whether, when, and how to enhance kelp

papers.abstract: Gene redundancy can complicate loss-of-function experiments (knockout), and its extent varies among organisms and biological functions. Relating variation in gene redundancy to the availability of genome-editing targets can help researchers select tractable biological functions and experimental organisms. Here, we present the transcript-aware Whole-genomic Evaluation for Editing Locus (tWhEEL), a pipeline that infers redundancy in silico from transcript information and cross-references it with specific guide RNA designs. tWhEEL integrates CRISPR-Cas9 guide design with Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway annotations to compute a knockout feasibility index (KFI) for individual genes and functional categories. Interactive HTML reports link GO-associated KFI and pathway-associated KFI summaries to the contributing groups, genes, and guide candidates with links to QuickGO or WikiPathways. By linking sequence-level guide candidates to functional-level targetability, tWhEEL can support the selection of biological functions and organisms for reverse-genetic experiments. Applications to model and nonmodel datasets revealed distinct targetability profiles, including high full targetability in yeast and query-protein-set dependence in zebrafish. A zebrafish Fanconi anemia case study recovered 14 of 19 published target-site designs. By connecting sequence-level guide candidates with function-level experimental planning, tWhEEL provides a framework for comparing reverse genetic tractability and prioritizing biological functions and organisms for further study.
papers.title: tWhEEL: a transcript-aware workflow for quantifying CRISPR knockout feasibility using transcriptome assembly

papers.abstract: Background and Aims: APOBEC-associated mutagenesis is prominent in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but genomic features associated with its intertumoral variability remain incompletely characterized. We investigated genomic correlates of APOBEC-associated mutagenesis while accounting for the compositional structure of mutational signature data. Methods: Mutational signatures were analyzed in 552 ESCC tumors from eight countries. APOBEC-associated mutagenesis was quantified as SBS2 plus SBS13 using absolute mutation counts and proportional contributions. Associations with co-occurring mutational signatures, total SBS burden, recurrent driver-gene alterations, and country were evaluated using correlation, sensitivity, and multivariable analyses. Principal component and regression-model robustness were additionally assessed. Results: APOBEC burden varied markedly across tumors (median, 2,002 mutations; IQR, 987-4,346). Several associations observed using signature proportions were not maintained in absolute-count analyses: SBS1, SBS3, and SBS5 changed direction, indicating sensitivity to compositional representation. In contrast, SBS18 remained inversely associated with APOBEC-associated mutagenesis in all variable pairings examined: proportion versus proportion (Spearman rho = -0.527), APOBEC proportion versus SBS18 absolute count (r = -0.435), and absolute count versus absolute count (Pearson r = -0.319, P = 1.59 x 10^-14; Spearman rho = -0.317). These are distinct comparisons rather than discrepant estimates. Notably, this cohort-wide relationship was primarily characterized by higher APOBEC burden in SBS18-negative than SBS18-positive tumors rather than a continuous inverse relationship among SBS18-positive tumors. The multivariable model had an in-sample R^2 of 0.400 but lower and variable 10-fold cross-validated performance (mean R^2 = 0.273). Country added little explanatory information to this model (delta R^2 = 0.008; global P = 0.402). ZNF750-mutant tumors had higher APOBEC burden than wild-type tumors (BH-FDR q = 0.0032), although only 12 tumors carried ZNF750 alterations. Conclusion: Genomic correlates of APOBEC-associated mutagenesis in ESCC are sensitive to the representation of mutational signature activity. SBS18 showed the most consistent inverse association, whereas the ZNF750 association warrants independent validation.
papers.title: Genomic Correlates of APOBEC-Associated Mutagenesis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

papers.abstract: Salamanders are an enduring and historically significant group that helped originate multiple scientific fields of study, including regeneration, cytogenetics, experimental embryology, cloning, evolutionary developmental biology and evolution of extreme genome size. We generated a high-quality, single haplotype assembly for the 32 Gb axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) genome using an F1 hybrid between axolotl and a divergent relative the tiger salamander (A. tigrinum). Using multi-genome alignments to other salamanders that meet VGP metrics, we leveraged strong conservation of karyotypic structure to identify >523,000 highly conserved non-coding elements within massively expanded intronic and intergenic regions, the vast majority of which are unique to the salamander lineage. Orthogonal measures of chromatin state and enhancer activity confirmed that many conserved elements correspond to cis-regulatory sequences and identified several thousand that are utilized during regeneration. The conserved elements identified here will enable robust functional genomic analyses of tissue regeneration and other traits that uniquely empower salamander models in biological research.
papers.title: Dissecting functional elements in giant genomes using the first generation of high quality salamander assemblies

papers.abstract: Podocyte cell differentiation in coordination with specialized endothelial cells forms the glomerulus, the kidney blood filter. Genetic analysis of animal models and human affected individuals has identified over 50 susceptibility genes that, when mutated, cause filtration defects or proteinuria. To explore the potential for new genetic pathways or components in glomerular development, we generated a transcriptome of micro-dissected three-day-post-fertilization zebrafish larval pronephric glomeruli and conducted a CRISPR-Cas9 G0 mutagenesis screen of less well characterized genes that showed glomerulus-enriched expression. Differential gene expression comparing glomeruli to whole larvae revealed a significant overlap of zebrafish glomerular-enriched gene expression with the human podocyte transcriptome. CRISPR-Cas9 G0 mutagenesis of twelve genes identified eight potential new causes of proteinuria in larval zebrafish based on glomerular leakage of rhodamine-labelled, 500 kDa high molecular weight dextran. Novel causes of proteinuria include regulators of small GTPases (fam49ba/cyrib, rasgrp3), cell adhesion/phosphatidylinositol metabolism (ptprq), and an upstream regulator of the hippo pathway (frmd6). Our glomerular transcriptome and screening results open new opportunities to explore glomerular cell differentiation and function.
papers.title: Novel regulators of zebrafish glomerular development

papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central feature of Down syndrome (DS), yet how trisomy 21 affects brain bioenergetics across scales--from gene transcription to cellular function to whole-brain metabolism--remains poorly understood. Here, we use the Dp16(1)Yey/+ (abbreviated Dp16) DS mouse model, which carries ~115 triplicated gene orthologs of human chromosome 21, to address this major knowledge gap and to provide direct in vivo evidence of brain-wide metabolic deficit in DS. Using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) approaches, we show that Dp16 mice have reduced cerebral blood flow and metabolic rate of oxygen, with effects more pronounced in males than in females. Despite the suppression of cerebral metabolic rate, mitochondrial respiratory capacity and ATP synthase activity are largely preserved across brain regions, with sex differences noted. Transcriptomic analyses reveal marked upregulation of mitochondrial OXPHOS genes and the convergence of biological pathways related to proteostasis and mitochondrial function across brain regions, with male cortex and female cerebellum showing the biggest change. Collectively, our data suggest that a brain-wide metabolic deficit in Dp16 mice triggers an adaptive mitochondrial remodeling program across the brain to support bioenergetic demands. This compensatory response, however, is insufficient to normalize the metabolic dysfunction in Dp16 mice. Our findings underscore the value of integrating functional assessments at the organismal and tissue levels with transcriptomic changes to gain a systems view of physiologic perturbations and adaptations in the DS brain which may influence phenotypic outcomes.
papers.title: Reduced cerebral blood flow and metabolic rate trigger an adaptive mitochondrial remodeling program in a Down syndrome mouse model

papers.abstract: Learning from large-scale bioactivity archives is complicated by heterogeneous assay readouts and differences in data reliability. Here we show that a model that predicts probability distributions over binding affinities from sequence data opens model training to vast and diverse troves of heterogeneous bioactivity data. We develop PSICHIC+, a bioactivity foundation model trained on approximately 82 million protein-ligand records using a distributional objective that preserves quantitative resolution while incorporating variation in data reliability. Given a protein sequence and ligand SMILES, PSICHIC+ predicts binding affinity in milliseconds. In zero-shot virtual-screening benchmarks without target-specific training data, it improves enrichment over regression- and classification-based approaches and performs competitively with leading structure-based methods. In lab-in-the-loop campaigns, distribution-guided acquisition improves recovery of high-activity compounds under fixed screening budgets. Combining PSICHIC+ with Boltz-2 improves hit-to-lead affinity prediction over Boltz-2 alone, with mean correlation approaching that of FEP+ on the evaluated benchmarks, without requiring high-resolution protein structures. These results support distributional learning as a scalable approach to using heterogeneous bioactivity data for hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization.
papers.title: Bioactivity foundation model for hit identification and hit-to-lead optimization from sequence data

papers.abstract: Structure-based interface predictors are normally reported as a single pooled ROC AUC over a residue test set. For a protein designer the operative question is different and much harder: given one target chain, will the top-ranked surface patch be a real binding site? We built EpiRank, a partner-agnostic epitope predictor, on HumanPPI 29,246 predicted human dimers, 12,296 target chains, 4.18 M residues using only single-chain geometry and physicochemistry (170 features, no partner, no sequence search, no structural alphabet), and evaluated it as a retrieval problem with homology- and partner-graph-controlled splits, on the 3,529 chains that survive an explicit partner-contamination filter. The model places a real epitope in its top-ranked patch 64 % of the time. That number is far less informative than it looks. Compact patches placed at random hit a real epitope 41 % of the time under the same rule, so the model's lift is 1.57 x, not 64 %; 54 % of all predicted patches land on nothing; and when the same chains are scored by models trained on a 2,000-chain and an 11,669-chain superset, a substantial fraction change answer while the aggregate barely moves. We document four specific ways this task invites overstatement partner-graph percolation across splits, single-linkage homology percolation at the conventional 30 % identity threshold, a count-only hit rule that rewards spatial smoothing rather than signal, and hotspot precision conditioned on success, which ranks a random baseline above the trained model. Each was hit during development and each inverted a conclusion we had already drawn. We argue that interface-prediction papers should report lift over a geometry-matched random baseline, patch precision, and per-target stability alongside AUC, and we release the evaluation harness that computes them.
papers.title: EpiRank: partner-agnostic surface-patch retrieval for epitope prediction of protein binding interfaces

papers.abstract: Many proteins that medicinal leeches package into salivary extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry no interpretable sequence annotation, so the least-characterised part of a pharmacologically important secretome lacks even a fold assignment. A companion Astral-DIA study of Hirudinaria manillensis nominated 17 ultra-enriched candidate EV cargo proteins. Here we ask whether structure prediction and structural search can assign folds where sequence methods fail, and which candidates remain unresolved under prespecified criteria. With an offline pipeline (ESMFold, TM-align, Foldseek against AFDB-SwissProt and PDB100, UniRef90 search, protein-to-genome alignment), the candidates separate into intracellular/membrane machinery and a secreted, cysteine-dense fraction of three proteins with no Pfam domain. The predicted structure of the leech Protein-sleepless homolog g21166 supports its assignment to the Ly-6/uPAR three-finger fold (TM 0.58 vs CD59; best significant PDB match Lynx1); no function is inferred. g436 and g20791 returned no match meeting the criterion (alnTM [≥] 0.5, E [≤] 0.05) in either database, g436 even after homolog-informed modelling. Gene structure and splice junctions support a conserved locus for the two-Trypsin-segment model g8114 (catalytic unit not established). A Boltz-2 thrombin pilot did not support target engagement, and a pre-registered nicotinic test was terminated as undecidable. The results yield a structure-informed shortlist for experimental follow-up.
papers.title: Structure-resolved fold annotation of the medicinal-leech salivary-EV cargo: a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger scaffold and a structurally dark fraction

papers.abstract: Tardigrades survive extreme environmental stress by expressing intrinsically disordered proteins that stabilize cellular structures during cryptobiosis. Because these proteins protect cells from desiccation, oxidative stress, and DNA damage, they have attracted interest as potential therapeutics to enhance stress resilience in other organisms. However, most studies have relied on cultured cells or germline expression, leaving their effects in somatic tissues largely unexplored. Here, we generated Caenorhabditis elegans strains expressing four tardigrade intrinsically disordered proteins, Damage Suppressor (DSUP), cytoplasmic-abundant heat-soluble (CAHS), mitochondrial-abundant heat-soluble (MAHS), and Ramazzottius varieornatus late embryogenesis abundant (RvLEAM), throughout somatic tissues. Surprisingly, constitutive expression of each protein reduced lifespan, impaired motility and reproduction, and failed to improve resistance to most environmental stressors. DSUP toxicity was tissue- and developmental stage-dependent, indicating that both spatial and temporal expression influence its physiological effects. Despite these detrimental phenotypes, several proteins reduced protein aggregation during desiccation-associated stress, demonstrating context-dependent protective effects. Together, our findings reveal that tardigrade stress proteins impose physiological tradeoffs in vivo and underscore the importance of evaluating candidate stress-protective proteins in physiologically relevant somatic models before therapeutic translation.
papers.title: Expression of tardigrade intrinsically disordered proteins in C. elegans reveals variable effects on aging and stress

papers.abstract: Hypermetabolism (elevated resting energy expenditure) is a hallmark of the pathophysiological response to burns. The contribution of wound excision to acute burn-induced hypermetabolism remains unclear. Importantly, while burn wound excision is a standard component of clinical burn care, it is not typically included in rodent models of burn injury. Here, we tested the hypothesis that burn wound excision drives the acute hypermetabolic response to burn trauma. C57BL/6J mice (n=12-18 per group; ~6-weeks old; 50% male) were acclimated to thermoneutral housing (30C) for 6-weeks. All mice underwent baseline body composition scans and metabolic phenotyping to determine total (TEE) and resting energy expenditure (REE). Mice were then randomized to either sham (control), scald burn (burn), wound excision (excision), or scald burn followed by immediate wound excision (burn+excision) groups. Burns and wound excisions involved ~15% of the body surface area. Mice then recovered for 14 days while individually housed in metabolic phenotyping cages. At day 14 post-injury, mice underwent a second body composition scan prior to euthanasia. There were no fatalities in the control or burn groups, whereas 23% (n=7) and 34% (n=11) of mice in the excision and burn+excision groups died or were euthanized during the 14-day recovery period. Male and female mice exhibited broadly similar responses to injury in terms of REE and TEE. Compared to control, REE was greater in burn (47%), excision (102%), and burn+excision groups (136%) during the first week post-injury (P<0.001 for all). Compared to control mice, wound excision (alone or following burns) resulted in a greater acute loss in body mass than burn injury alone. However, this cachectic response was more sustained in male mice compared to females. Similarly, wound excision (alone or following burns) resulted in greater bone mineral content and density loss compared to sham and burn alone in both sexes. Wound excision is a key contributor to the hypermetabolic and cachectic response to burn trauma in mice. We posit that rodent studies aiming to recapitulate burn-induced hypermetabolism and cachexia should include burn wound excision to better model the clinical sequelae to burns.
papers.title: Burn Wound Excision Drives Acute Hypermetabolism in Mice with Scald Burns

papers.abstract: Predation is a potent driver of behavioral divergence across prey populations, yet whether shared predation regimes generate similar responses in coexisting prey species remains unclear. Species differences in reproductive and foraging traits may alter vulnerability to predators, generating species-specific responses. We compared behavior and cognition of two poeciliid fishes (Gambusia affinis and Poecilia latipinna) that differ in body size, the presence of male ornamentation, and mating tactics. We sampled both species across replicate high- and low-predation regimes and measured exploration, shyness, boldness, social motivation, and detour solve latency (N = 509). Multivariate behavior and cognition differed between predation regimes, and the magnitude of divergence varied with species but not body size. Consistent with the multivariate pattern, the more conspicuous P. latipinna exhibited higher boldness and overall lower exploration under high-predation, while high- and low-predation populations of G. affinis did not differ. These findings suggest either that the more conspicuous species experiences greater predation risk or that the less conspicuous species reduces its predation risk through alternative phenotypic responses. More broadly, species differences in reproductive phenotypes associated with sexual selection may help explain why shared predation regimes generate variable patterns of behavioral divergence across taxa.
papers.title: Behavioral divergence across replicated predation regimes is species-specific in two sympatric poeciliid fishes

papers.abstract: MRI studies have mapped the atrophic signature that distinguishes Alzheimer's disease (AD), isolating regions differentially vulnerable to its age-dependent neurodegenerative process. An endosomal recycling pathway regulated by the interaction of SORL1 with retromer is pathogenically disrupted in AD. Here we test the hypothesis, that the pathway might drive the neurodegenerative process, via multiple yearlong studies in over 140 wildtype and SORL1 deficient mice, modeling SORL1's causative mutations. MRI studies revealed that SORL1 deficiency induced an age-dependent AD-pattern of atrophy, centered on the trans-entorhinal cortex, and that atrophy was prevented by SORL1 restoration, secondary to overexpressing the retromer protein VPS26b. Postmortem studies validated that the atrophy reflects neuronal loss. Proteomic profiling revealed that the atrophy is associated with reductions in cell death suppressors, one of which was then found deficient in the trans-entorhinal cortex of AD patients. Besides supporting the hypothesis, when taken together with other findings the results suggest that SORL1-retromer disruptions represent a therapeutically-amenable common 'neurodegeneration pathway' in AD.
papers.title: Disrupting SORL1-retromer endosomal recycling in mice drives the age-dependent neurodegenerative signature of Alzheimer's disease

papers.abstract: Resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) originate from multiple fetal hematopoietic waves and seed organs during the prenatal window where they acquire tissue-specific homeostatic functions. Several growth factors within the fetal niche are required for RTM development, but knowledge of how these signals program tissue-specific RTM survival, identity, and function during the prenatal window is limited. Here, we investigated the functional role of developmental IL7/IL7R signaling on fetal RTM survival and function. IL7 deficiency impaired neonatal RTM establishment, similar to IL7R deficiency, and IL7 was broadly expressed in fetal tissues and co-localized with IL7R+ macrophages. IL7/IL7R signaling regulated cell cycle, apoptotic, and inflammatory transcriptional pathways and activated phospho-AKT signaling in fetal liver myeloid cells. IL7R deletion impaired proliferation of fetal liver monocyte precursors and increased fetal liver macrophage apoptosis. Specific Cre-mediated IL7R deletion in fetal definitive HSC-derived, but not EMP- derived, macrophages caused irrecoverable postnatal loss of IL7R-expressing macrophages in specific tissues, including the liver, demonstrating a specific temporal requirement for IL7R expression during fetal myelopoiesis. Prenatal IL7R blockade subsequently impaired adaptive responses to chronic fibrotic liver injury in adulthood, associated with increased monocyte infiltration and upregulation of pro-inflammatory signaling pathways. These findings redefine IL7 as a developmental myeloid niche factor and demonstrate that IL7/IL7R signaling is co-opted during fetal development to imprint durable RTM programs that shape postnatal tissue immunity and adaptive responses to injury.
papers.title: Developmental IL7/IL7R signaling in fetal resident tissue macrophages regulates adaptive responses to liver injury

papers.abstract: Objectives: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multi-organ autoimmune disease for which no broadly effective disease-modifying treatment exists. We developed an integrated multi-organ single-cell atlas of SSc to identify shared and organ specific disease-associated transcriptional programmes and potential therapeutic targets. Methods: We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from skin, lung, synovium, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (six studies, 401,902 cells, 90 individuals) using Harmony. Pseudobulk differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis were performed at the tissue cell-compartment, cell-type, and subpopulation levels, including independent reclustering of lymphoid, myeloid and fibroblast populations. Results: Disease-associated transcriptional programmes showed marked tissue dependence, even within the same cell lineage, highlighting the importance of organ-specific mechanisms in SSc. Nevertheless, recurrent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling programmes were identified in lung, skin and synovium, and interferon signalling programmes in skin, synovium and peripheral blood mononuclear cells, across immune and fibroblast cell populations. Although no subpopulation was exclusive to SSc, a shared myofibroblast subpopulation expressing SFRP2, COL1A1, POSTN, ACTA2, and COMP was identified across lung, skin, and synovium. In addition, perivascular and mitotic fibroblast subpopulations exhibited both profibrotic and inflammatory signatures, including interferon- and IL-2-related signalling programmes. Conclusions: SSc is characterised by two complementary axes: a tissue-dependent cellular programme and a recurrent fibrotic and interferon-associated signature extending across multiple organs and cell populations. These findings are consistent with current organ-based therapeutic approaches while highlighting interferon signalling as a potential multi-organ therapeutic target. The resulting interactive single-cell atlas provides a resource for investigating shared and organ-specific disease mechanisms and guiding future therapeutic research.
papers.title: Development of a multi-organ single-cell atlas of systemic sclerosis reveals shared and tissue-specific pathogenic pathways.

papers.abstract: Sexual reproduction is critical in most eukaryotes, but many genes required for the process remain to be identified and characterized. A previous saturation mutagenesis study in Schizosaccharomyces pombe implicated several unnamed genes in having roles in sexual reproduction. In this work, we provide an initial characterization of 13 of these genes and an in-depth characterization of one gene, fss1 (facilitates starvation sex). Fss1 has high structural homology to the human PQ-loop repeat family PQLC2 transceptor (amino acid transporter plus membrane receptor), but likely lacks the ability to transport amino acids due to loss of a critical PQ motif. fss1{Delta} mutants have no defects in meiosis but have pronounced defects in packaging the products of meiosis into spores, particularly in nutrient-poor environments. The spore formation phenotypes are recessive as fss1{Delta} spores produced by a fss1+/fss1{Delta} heterozygote develop normally. Immuno-gold electron microscopy shows Fss1 localizes to vesicles that fuse to the ephemeral outer spore membrane as the spore wall matures below. Fss1 protein is also produced within spores and this population is required for normal vacuole morphology and timely germination. We propose a model in which Fss1 is a vesicle receptor that facilitates spore wall formation from diploid-expressed protein, while spore-expressed protein acts at the vacuole to promote an internal cellular environment that facilitates germination. This work expands our catalog of genes that contribute to sexual reproduction and identifies two previously unknown tasks in spore biology that are both facilitated by Fss1.
papers.title: Fss1, a CTNS/PQ domain protein, has dual roles in promoting fertility in Schizosaccharomyces pombe

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) tumors with a high migration-to-proliferation ratio (D/k) are associated with treatment resistance, motivating the estimation of D/k from routine pre-treatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data and the investigation of mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity across patients. Unlike previous approaches based on nested spherical approximations of enhancing and non-enhancing tumor volumes, we incorporate the spatial arrangement of the enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions by deriving a 1D tumor density distribution from their segmentations and fitting a 1D reaction-diffusion model to estimate D/k. We achieved an error of under 5% when comparing our method to synthetic density distributions and found excellent correlation with synthetic tumor segmentations (Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) = 0.996). We then evaluated associations between patient-specific D/k values and their clinical, transcriptomic, and radiomic features. When applied to 102 pre-treatment MRI scans from the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2017 dataset, elevated D/k significantly correlated with reduced overall survival (log-rank p = 0.01), older age (p = 0.04), and a trend toward lower Karnofsky Performance Status (p = 0.059). In a subset of 91 patients with available microarray data, mesenchymal-like phenotypes consistently exhibited elevated D/k across three established molecular subtype classifications (p = 0.013, p = 0.055, and p = 0.127). Elastic Net regularization followed by overrepresentation analysis revealed an enrichment of glycosylation-related pathways among genes associated with D/k variability (p = 0.0123 and p = 0.0368). Furthermore, Multi-Omic Factor Analysis identified a radiomic factor correlated with D/k (r = 0.57, p = 4x10-9), with the highest-weighted features corresponding to smoothness of the non-enhancing tumor region on T2 and FLAIR.
papers.title: Estimating glioblastoma migration-to-proliferation ratio from single time-point MRI data via radial density distribution

papers.abstract: The generation of paediatric musculoskeletal models often requires compromise between data availability, accuracy, and computation time. Statistical shape models allow for rapid generation of bone geometries for use in musculoskeletal modelling. An articulated shape model allows for movement at the joints during optimisation to better fit to experimental data. Here we present a methodology for generating custom paediatric OpenSim models using an articulated shape model of the lower limb generated from CT scans of over 300 children aged 4 to 18 years old. Bone geometries are predicted using demographic factors (age, height, mass, and sex), linear bone measurements (bone widths and lengths), and 12 skin surface landmarks (L/R ASIS, L/R PSIS, medial/lateral epicondyles, and medial/lateral malleoli). To account for skin padding (bone to skin surface distance) a random forest algorithm was developed for skin padding prediction for these 12 landmarks. Accuracy of the model prediction was assessed using a leave-one-out analysis to assess landmark errors, bone surface errors, and clinical bone measurement errors (linear measurements and angular values). Motion capture and MRI data were collected from two paediatric test cases to test the workflow on unseen data. Skin padding values varied widely in this population with average values from 3.4mm at the lateral malleolus to 25.9mm at the PSIS. Skin padding was best predicted using age, height, mass, ASIS width, epicondylar width, and malleolar width with an average RMSE of 4.68mm. The articulated shape model predicted accurate bone geometries from skin surface landmarks with average bone surface RMSEs of 2.64 {+/-} 0.99mm, 1.91 {+/-} 0.59mm, and 1.69 {+/-} 0.56mm in the pelvis, femora, and tibiae/fibulae respectively. In the two unseen test cases, average bone surface errors ranged from 1.64 {+/-} 1.2mm to 3.41 {+/-} 3.1mm. This study demonstrated the accuracy of "MiniMAP", for the rapid generation of custom paediatric musculoskeletal models.
papers.title: MiniMAP: An automatic pipeline for paediatric lower limb musculoskeletal model generation

papers.abstract: The Vedda people are regarded as the direct descendants of Sri Lanka's Mesolithic hunter-gatherers and represent one of South Asia's oldest surviving indigenous populations. X-chromosomal short tandem repeat (X-STR) analysis provides a powerful framework to examine their genetic distinctiveness, as the X chromosome exhibits sex-biased biparental inheritance and greater sensitivity to demographic and evolutionary forces compared to autosomal markers. However, no X-STR-based genetic investigations have yet been conducted on this population. In the present study, we successfully genotyped 50 unrelated Veddas individuals using a recently developed 16 X-STR multiplex PCR system optimized for Sri Lankan populations. Our analyses revealed a statistically significant genetic differentiation (2.43%) between the Veddas and the principal local ethnic groups; Sinhalese, Sri Lankan Tamils, Indian Tamils, and Moors exceeding previous estimates based on autosomal STR markers. Comparative analysis with 32 global populations positioned the Veddas as a genetically distinct and isolated group, separated from clusters representing South Asians, Europeans, Middle Easterners, and other indigenous populations such as Australian Aboriginals, Bhil Indians, and Kedayans, emphasizing their unique genetic heritage. Reduced allelic (115) and haplotype (62) counts, alongside significant linkage disequilibrium detected among eight pairs of X-STR loci, reflect the influence of genetic drift within this small, endogamous, and historically isolated population. These findings highlight the evolutionary and demographic distinctiveness of the Veddas and provide essential baseline data for future population genomic studies. Furthermore, the demonstrated high discriminatory power of the 16 X-STR loci supports their continued application in population genetics and anthropological research within this unique community.
papers.title: X-Chromosomal STR-based analysis of genetic diversity, structure, and phylogeny in the Sri Lankan Vedda population

papers.abstract: Physical forces dictate the function and maintenance of adult musculoskeletal tissues. Yet, the impact of biophysical cues on the growth and maturation of these tissues, especially dense connective tissues, remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of neonatal mechanical loading on early postnatal growth of the musculoskeletal tissues of the lower limb, with particular focus on the Achilles tendon. We performed sciatic nerve resection (SNR) on one-day-old mice to denervate the hamstrings and distal hindlimb muscles. Sciatic Nerve Resection resulted in severe and sustained alterations in gait, accompanied by an altered transcriptional landscape in distal musculoskeletal tissues, with marked reductions in bone and tendon growth and smaller, fibrotic hindlimb musculature. Sciatic nerve resection impaired cumulative growth in the Achilles tendon, shifting cell proliferation and matrix-driven growth trajectories and altering mechanotransduction gene programs toward inflammation and matrix catabolism with age. This work highlights the essential role of mechanical loading in driving mechanosignaling and postnatal growth trajectories in musculoskeletal tissues of the developing limb, with implications for overall musculoskeletal health in adulthood.
papers.title: Impaired loading following denervation elicits dynamic, differential growth trajectories of musculoskeletal tissues

papers.abstract: Understanding how the human brain matures from infancy through adolescence is essential for identifying factors that influence health outcomes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides powerful tools for characterizing structural, microstructural, functional, and metabolic aspects of brain development; however, many pediatric imaging studies are constrained by small sample sizes, limited geographic diversity, lack of longitudinal measurement, restricted age ranges, and heterogeneous acquisition protocols. While recent large-scale neuroimaging consortia have begun to address these challenges, such resources remain limited in the Canadian context, creating a critical gap. The Canadian Pediatric Imaging Platform (C-PIP) has developed a multisite neuroimaging framework across three of Canada's largest pediatric hospitals: Alberta Children's Hospital (Calgary), Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sainte-Justine (Montreal), and the Hospital for Sick Children (Toronto). These three sites were united through a national initiative, leveraging high-performance MRI systems to accelerate Canadian neurodevelopmental research. In addition, C-PIP has implemented a centralized data sharing infrastructure to facilitate open science and collaborative research across institutions. Here, we describe the development and implementation of a multimodal MRI acquisition protocol designed to support multimodal longitudinal studies of typical and atypical brain development spanning infancy through adolescence. Within-site stability and cross-site stability of C-PIP core MRI sequences were evaluated using a travelling-participant study. The C-PIP MRI protocol establishes a harmonized, multisite imaging framework that supports large-scale investigations of pediatric brain development and disorders.
papers.title: The Canadian Pediatric Imaging Platform (C-PIP) Reference Sample: Neuroimaging Protocol and Cross-site Validation for Harmonized Multimodal Pediatric Imaging

papers.abstract: Synapse loss is a major correlate of cognitive decline in neurodegenerative disease, yet its relationship to localized pathology remains difficult to study at scale. Conventional confocal imaging approaches are limited by low throughput, selection bias, and restricted sampling of pathological features. Here, we describe an automated high-content imaging and analysis workflow that enables large-scale quantification of amyloid beta plaque-associated synapse loss within mouse brain tissue. Using Preciscan-based multiscale acquisition on the Opera Phenix platform, this workflow combines tissue-wide pathology mapping with targeted high-magnification imaging and subcellular analysis. We apply this framework to acquire and analyze hundreds of plaque images in the CRND8 mouse model of A{beta} proteinopathy, demonstrating plaque-associated synapse loss within developing plaque populations over disease progression. We find that small diffuse plaques accumulate rapidly at late stages in CRND8, but that the primary synapse loss comes from large cored plaques. More broadly, this scalable framework enables systematic investigation of subcellular phenomena across pathological microenvironments in disease models.
papers.title: Automated multiscale high-content imaging connects plaque population heterogeneity to localized synapse loss

papers.abstract: Peripheral neuroblastic tumors (pNTs) are embryonal tumors of neural crest origin with highly variable clinical behaviors, ranging from spontaneous regression to aggressive and fatal disease. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC) defines four diagnostic categories and stratifies tumors into Favorable Histology (FH) or Unfavorable Histology (UH) group based on age-linked assessment of tumor differentiation/maturation and the Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index (MKI). Prognostic distinction according to INPC offers significant prediction of clinical outcomes, with patients harboring FH tumors demonstrating longer overall and event-free survival than those with UH tumor. Here, we assembled the largest multi-continental whole-slide histology imaging dataset of pNTs to date, comprising 2,030 tumors from the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany and Japan. Using this dataset, we developed NB-PathAssist, a computational pathology framework for automated INPC-based classification from digitized whole-slide images. NB-PathAssist integrates foundation-model-based feature extraction with an archetype-guided SummaryMixing architecture that compresses whole-slide morphology into representative histologic tokens for tumor-level classification. To automate MKI assessment, we manually annotated 14,049 nuclei, classifying them as mitotic-karyorrhectic (MK) tumor cells, non-MK tumor cells, or non-tumor cells. The resulting model was applied to phenotype cells in whole-slide images across 1,649 tissue sections. Across geographically and institutionally diverse cohorts, NB-PathAssist reproducibly assessed key diagnostic features and generated prognostic classifications concordant with reference INPC annotations. The average balanced accuracy for classifying tumor categories, grade of neuroblastic differentiation, MKI and prognostic groups achieved 0.84, 0.86, 0.89 and 0.96, respectively. We packaged the NB-PathAssist algorithms into an end-to-end online platform for scalable and standardized AI-assisted assessment of pNTs.
papers.title: Digital pathological classification of peripheral neuroblastic tumors across multi-continent cohorts

papers.abstract: Metastasis, the dissemination of cancer cells to distant organs, is an inefficient process1, yet remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality2. The cellular barriers and evasion mechanisms governing organ-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood3-5, hindering the development of effective anti-metastatic therapies6. Here, we show that liver-resident type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s) constitute an essential immunosurveillance barrier against breast cancer liver metastasis that can be bypassed through either cancer cell intrinsic or host-dependent mechanisms. In a multi-organ metastatic breast cancer patient cohort, liver metastasis occurred later and was associated with poorer survival than lung metastasis, with elevated body mass index emerging as a clinical risk factor. This metabolic vulnerability was recapitulated in mice, where a high-fat diet induced hepatosteatosis and selectively enhanced breast cancer colonization of the liver. Mechanistically, liver and lung colonization were restrained by ILC1s and circulating natural killer (NK) cells, respectively. Following cancer cell challenge, NK cells expanded and activated, employing lytic granule pathways and the death receptor DR5 for clearance, whereas activated ILC1s selectively required high DR5 expression on cancer cells, supported by AP-2a (TFAP2A) mediated transcriptional activation, for effective immunosurveillance. Heterozygous copy number deletion at TNFRSF10B (encoding DR5) in human tumours reduced DR5 expression and predisposed to liver metastasis. Hepatosteatosis further compromised this barrier by reducing IL-15 expression in macrophages, thereby depleting hepatic ILC1s effects reversible with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists. Thus, hepatic ILC1s form a critical organ-specific barrier to breast cancer metastasis, vulnerable to both cancer cell-intrinsic DR5 downregulation and host metabolic dysfunction.
papers.title: Evasion of Hepatic ILC1 Immunosurveillance Drives Breast Cancer Liver Metastasis

papers.abstract: Motor cortex acquires skilled movements through recurrent spiking dynamics and experience-dependent synaptic plasticity, yet how such circuits learn continuous motor control using biologically local signals remains unclear. Here, we develop a recurrent spiking neural network model of motor cortex that addresses both the computational and biological requirements of motor learning. We first analytically derived the recurrent firing-rate state directly from synaptic input and trained the network by implicit differentiation, thereby avoiding backpropagation through long spike trajectories. We then introduced State-Carry Initialization, which enables closed-loop motor control by continuously carrying the ongoing recurrent state across successive actions. Building on this formulation, we devised a learning rule termed Feedback-Spike Nudging (FSN), in which teaching signals are delivered as spikes through a feedback pathway. Synaptic changes depend only on presynaptic activity and the feedback-evoked change in postsynaptic firing, consistent with biological mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in motor cortex. The resulting networks learned continuous motor control through both supervised and reinforcement learning, which could be mapped respectively onto interactions of motor cortex with the cerebellum and basal ganglia. Moreover, the FSN learning rule was consistent with experimental observations of structural spine plasticity in mouse motor cortex. Thus, our study lays a foundation for recurrent spiking models of motor cortex that are biologically grounded at both the functional and anatomical levels.
papers.title: Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks for Continuous Motor Control: A Biologically Plausible Model of Motor Cortex

papers.abstract: The airways of people with cystic fibrosis (CF) are colonized by a polymicrobial community and coinfections with multiple pathogens may exacerbate disease. By analyzing 16S rRNA gene sequencing datasets, we determined that Achromobacter-Pseudomonas coinfection was associated with worse lung function than infection with either pathogen alone, or coinfections with Pseudomonas and other CF bacterial pathogens. We discovered Achromobacter spp. induced production of the siderophore pyoverdine by Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain PAO1 and other clinical isolates on synthetic CF sputum medium (SCFM), supplemented with physiologically relevant iron concentrations. We then tested 21 Achromobacter strains, encompassing seven species, and determined that 17 (81%) induced pyoverdine production. We sequenced the full genomes of these Achromobacter and found 18 (86%) encoded a biosynthetic gene cluster for the production of alcaligin. This compound is an iron-chelating siderophore that has previously been shown to be involved in colonization of the respiratory tract by Bordetella spp. Using mass spectrometry imaging, we confirmed that Achromobacter dolens strain RMS0405 produces alcaligin during coculture with PAO1. Further, we found that supplementing SCFM with increasing iron abolishes pyoverdine induction by PAO1 during coculture. Pyoverdine is known to contribute directly to virulence and regulate expression of other virulence factors. Using transcriptomics and proteomics, we determined that RMS0405 induces a low-iron stress response in PAO1 and stimulates the production of exotoxin A and other known virulence factors. Together, our results indicate that Achromobacter spp. and P. aeruginosa may exacerbate virulence in the airways of people with CF as a byproduct of competition for iron.
papers.title: Siderophore-Mediated Competition Between Cystic Fibrosis Pathogens Increases Virulence Factor Production

papers.abstract: As events unfold, they carry structure in both their timing and content, with these dimensions often interrelated. Most research has treated these dimensions separately, although processing them jointly may provide important computational benefits. It is an open question whether the brain processes a sequence's timing and predictable content structure independently, or integrates these two sources of information to guide prediction. We hypothesised that predictable timing would allow listeners to better exploit structure in the content, with this effect increasing as content structure becomes stronger. To test this, we presented tone sequences with pitch trajectories following a 1/f^{beta} structure, where {beta} determines how strongly the content of each tone persists, while independently varying the temporal periodicity of the sequence. Performance was quantified using response errors relative to outcome predictions of a Gaussian Process Regression model and a model-free measure of how strongly preceding tones influenced responses. Response error decreased and reliance on preceding tones increased with higher {beta} and periodic timing. Moreover, the influence of preceding tones showed an interaction between timing and content, such that the effect of periodicity grew with increasing {beta}. The response error showed no such interaction, although the effect of periodic timing was reliable only for the most structured sequences. Our findings suggest an interdependency between content and timing, where predictable timing helps listeners make greater use of predictable content.
papers.title: Predictable Timing Enhances the Use of Predictable Content

papers.abstract: In the digestive tract of neonatal mammals and in fish, lysosome-rich enterocytes (LREs) internalize dietary proteins and digest them intracellularly within a large lysosomal vacuole. Impaired LRE function leads to growth stunting and poor survival in zebrafish and mice. Previous work has shown that protein uptake relies on a scavenger receptor complex. However, how LREs can internalize proteins rapidly enough to support organismal growth is unclear. Here, using live and electron microscopy and genetic manipulations in zebrafish, we find that LREs contain apical micron-sized clathrin-coated endocytic tubules (ETs) that allow for the concentration and rapid internalization of soluble protein cargoes, while excluding resident apical membrane proteins.
